**Comparison of Official Teams Integration Roadmap vs. Informal Sales/Slack Claims**

**Official Roadmap (Source of Truth):** The Microsoft Teams integration is strictly in the "Active Design and Planning" phase, with a release target of **Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)**. A restricted pilot will begin in **October 2026** with selected financial/healthcare accounts to validate security isolation. Currently, only the Slack connector is available as a limited pilot. [NL-014-S07] This roadmap status is explicitly reaffirmed as the authoritative source by Product (Sofia Almeida), CTO (Leon Grayson), and Infrastructure (Raj), who state that development has not started and the feature is slated for design in Q4 2026. [NL-027-S04] [NL-015-S06] [NL-027-S03]

**Informal Sales Claims:** VP Sales Marcus Reed makes multiple overclaims. In a customer call, he tells Michael Chang the integration is "basically right around the corner," "almost ready for general release," and "basically done," promising it for a July pilot. [NL-023-S04] He also told prospect Apex Global Solutions the feature is "basically right around the corner." [NL-027-S02] He pushes for a July/August pilot and requests packaging an insecure "toy" demo as an 'alpha' or a custom hardcoded build. [NL-027-S04] [NL-015-S06]

**Informal Slack/Engineering Reality:** The internal Slack thread directly contradicts these claims. Engineering (Chloe and Raj) confirm the only existing demo is a "toy" webhook script with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and no formatting/citations. [NL-027-S03] They explicitly state the roadmap is the source of truth and refuse to release insecure features into production. [NL-027-S04] Also, the Sales Playbook (NL-009) explicitly warns that promising the Teams integration as "almost ready" is incorrect—the roadmap shows it in planning/design for Q4 2026—and directs reps to consult the official roadmap. [NL-009-S08]

**Conflict Resolution:** The official Product Roadmap (NL-014) holds higher authority than the sales playbook (NL-009, which is explicitly labeled Authority Level 2) and informal Slack narratives. NL-014 explicitly notes that formal "Sales and Slack Contradiction" warnings are required to correct the "almost ready" claims. [NL-014-S07] The internal Slack and CTO/Product statements further validate the roadmap as the binding source. Therefore, the informal sales claims of immediate readiness or July/August availability are overclaims contradicted by the official roadmap, engineering capacity, and security policy. The mobile web workaround is suggested as an interim solution. [NL-027-S04]
